# Photometric and Image Reconstruction Losses

Also called: Composite Image Loss, Composite Photometric and Regularization Loss

## Overview
This family defines the objective functions used to supervise differentiable volume rendering and splatting by comparing rendered images against ground-truth observations. It solves the ill-posed nature of inverse rendering by balancing color fidelity against geometric and structural priors. It sets itself apart from standard photometric losses by explicitly incorporating visibility weighting [4262-composite-image-loss-with-visibility-weighting.md] and a broad suite of regularization terms (opacity, distortion, normal, size, flow, and total variation) [9355-composite-photometric-and-regularization-loss.md].

## Shared principles
The total loss $\mathcal{L}$ is a weighted sum of photometric reconstruction errors and regularization terms. The photometric component typically combines L1 loss and SSIM (Structural Similarity Index) loss, sometimes augmented with perceptual metrics like LPIPS (Learned Perceptual Image Patch Similarity). Regularization terms enforce constraints on the underlying representation, such as density sparsity, geometric smoothness, or primitive shape validity. The specific formulation depends on whether the representation is implicit (grids/volumes) or explicit (primitives/splats).

## Subtopics

### [Composite Image Loss with Visibility Weighting](4262-composite-image-loss-with-visibility-weighting.md)
This method computes a composite photometric loss $\mathcal{L}_c$ by weighting pixel-wise reconstruction errors with a visibility map $\mathbf{V}_M$. It solves the problem of supervising rendered images $\mathbf{I}_r$ against ground-truth images $\mathbf{I}_{gt}$ in scenarios where occlusion or transparency makes naive pixel-wise comparison ineffective. It sets itself apart from standard photometric losses by explicitly masking the L1 and SSIM terms with visibility weights, while retaining an unweighted perceptual term, and is defined in [4262-composite-image-loss-with-visibility-weighting.md].

### [Composite Photometric and Regularization Loss](9355-composite-photometric-and-regularization-loss.md)
This method defines the total objective function for optimizing differentiable volume rendering or splatting representations by combining photometric reconstruction errors with various geometric and structural regularization terms. It solves the ill-posed nature of inverse rendering by balancing color fidelity against priors such as opacity sparsity, geometric distortion, normal consistency, and spatial smoothness. It differs from its sibling [Composite Image Loss with Visibility Weighting](4262-composite-image-loss-with-visibility-weighting.md) by explicitly incorporating a broader suite of regularization terms (opacity, distortion, normal, size, flow, and total variation) rather than focusing primarily on visibility-based weighting of the photometric term.

### Composite RGB and Entropy Loss
This variant combines RGB reconstruction loss with entropy regularization on the foreground accumulated alpha value to encourage opaque rendering.
#### formula
- The RGB loss is defined as [S1]:
  $$ \mathcal {L}_{\mathrm {rgb}}=\left (1-\lambda _r\right ) \mathcal {L}_1+\lambda _r \mathcal {L}_{\mathrm {ssim}} $$
  where $\mathcal{L}_1$ is L1 loss, $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{ssim}}$ is SSIM loss, and $\lambda_r$ is the weight.
- The entropy loss is defined as [S1]:
  $$ \mathcal {L}_{\text {entropy}}=-\sum \left (\mathbf {O}_{\text {fg}}\log \mathbf {O}_{\text {fg}}+\left (1-\mathbf {O}_{\text {fg}}\right ) \log \left (1-\mathbf {O}_{\text {fg}}\right )\right ) $$
  where $\mathbf{O}_{\text{fg}}$ is the foreground accumulated alpha value.
- The total loss is defined as [S1]:
  $$ \mathcal {L}=\left (1-\lambda _r\right ) \mathcal {L}_1+\lambda _r \mathcal {L}_{\mathrm {ssim}}+\lambda _e \mathcal {L}_{\text {entropy}} $$
#### parameter
- $\lambda_r$: Weight for SSIM loss in RGB loss. Value: 0.2 [S1].
- $\lambda_e$: Weight for entropy loss. Value: 0.1 [S1].

## Background
The use of L1 and SSIM losses for volume rendering supervision is standard in NeRF-based methods. The integration of entropy regularization on alpha values to encourage opacity is described in [S1]. The composite loss structures combining photometric terms with geometric regularizations (distortion, normal, size) are prevalent in Gaussian Splatting and primitive-based rendering methods [9355-composite-photometric-and-regularization-loss.md].

## Sources
[S1] EVolSplat: Efficient Volume-based Gaussian Splatting for Urban View Synthesis, https://doi.org/10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.01054, fetched 2026-11-03
